author: Milwaukee City Wire
title: Milwaukee Public Schools plans events for Historically Black Colleges and Universities Week
text:
Dr. Keith P. Posley Superintendent at Milwaukee Public Schools | Official website
Dr. Keith P. Posley Superintendent at Milwaukee Public Schools | Official website
Milwaukee Public Schools (MPS) will observe Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU) Week from November 10 to 14, 2025. The week is designed to help students learn about college and career options, with a focus on HBCUs.
During the week, MPS staff are encouraged to wear clothing representing HBCUs or Greek organizations. Students will participate in activities aimed at preparing them for higher education and professional paths.
On Monday, students are advised to explore scholarships, internships, and other financial resources through the United Negro College Fund and Thurgood Marshall Fund websites. Graduating seniors are also reminded that completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) is required for graduation. FAFSA provides information about available grants and loans.
Tuesday’s activities include a virtual tour of HBCUs and visiting the district’s dedicated HBCU webpage at mpsmke.com/hbcuweek.
On Wednesday, high school students and their parents can attend a UNCF Parent Workshop online. Registration is available through the event link provided by MPS.
Thursday features the UNCF Empower Me Tour for high school students. This event covers topics such as colleges, financial aid, and scholarships. Students seeking more information are encouraged to contact their school counselors.
Friday offers an opportunity for students to learn about African-American Greek Letter Organizations that promote academic achievement and equity by visiting their website.
"College and career planning is part of every student’s education journey in Milwaukee Public Schools," according to an official statement from the district. "From November 10–14, 2025, the district will highlight Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). Students can expect a variety of activities throughout the week and should plan to take part."
A complete list of events planned for HBCU Week can be found at https://mpsmke.com/hbcuweek.
